issue_context.title: shorthand condition in action block not valid?
issue_context.body: ### The problem seems the new shorthand conditions are not accepted in the config checker ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? 2022.5.0.dev20220427 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue automation ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/automation/ ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml - alias: Timer switch id: timer_switch trigger: platform: state entity_id: input_boolean.test action: - not: - condition: state entity: input_boolean.test_2 state: 'on' ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? ```txt Logger: homeassistant.config Source: config.py:454 First occurred: 23:07:10 (1 occurrences) Last logged: 23:07:10 Invalid config for [automation]: Unable to determine action @ data['action'][0]. Got None. (See ?, line ?). ``` ### Additional information tbh, I am not sure of the correct syntax,(do we need the leading 'condition' or not) but any regular condition I tested in the condition block was refused in an action block config check passes with a valid config... though the logs shows other wise
comments:
[script documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/script)
[script source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/script)
<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Hey there @home-assistant/core, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`script`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L872) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
CC  @thomasloven

You're fast.... I was still trying to add this:

```
Invalid config for [automation]: Unexpected value for condition: '[OrderedDict([('not', [OrderedDict([('condition', 'state'), ('entity', 'input_boolean.test_2'), ('state', 'on')])])])]'. Expected and, device, not, numeric_state, or, state, sun, template, time, trigger, zone, a list of conditions or a valid template @ data['action'][0]. Got None. (See ?, line ?).
```

which happens when trying:
```
    action:
      - condition:
          - not:
              - condition: state
                entity: input_boolean.test_2
                state: 'on'
```

or
```
    action:
      - condition:
          not:
            - condition: state
              entity: input_boolean.test_2
              state: 'on'
```

might be missing the obvious but it keeps erroring.

I don't see a way to easily support shorthand conditions in action blocks directly without making it very complicated. If anything, we should support it _under_ `condition:` but that's not how conditions work today.

The error in the second post is because it should be `entity_id`, not `entity`.

`and:` `or` and `not` are not allowed outside of a `condition` by choice, because I thought that would be confusing.
I believe the documentation reflects this IIRC, but I'll double check.

> because I thought that would be confusing.

Is it? I think it's more confusing if it isn't consistent.

I don't see why: 

```yaml
- condition: or
  conditions:
    ...
```

Would be allowed as action, but not:

```yaml
- or:
  ....
```

Additionally, you have explicitly extended the `CONDITION_ACTION_SCHEMA`:

See: <https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/70120/files#diff-f9f84381af1676630c88469d5fb4f69f36934019ffbbf187b78f9c976f03cae4R1401>

This makes me highly doubt this not working intentionally.

> I don't see a way to easily support shorthand conditions in action blocks directly without making it very complicated. 

I think its a one line patch though. Will try/test.
It is one line change: Will write up some tests to make sure it works as intended and open up a PR to get review/decision on it.

Have to run but
```yaml
- condition:
    or:
      - a
      - b
```
Was the idea in that case.

That makes it clear what the purpose of the block is - to check whether a condition is fulfilled.

IMO that isn't conveyed by
```yaml
- or:
  - a
  - b
```

That is a good example with which I have to agree. Let's document it explicitly in that case.

EDIT: I'm still not 100% positive though, as in, we can still document the clear variant. I still do think its inconsistent.

For reference, this was the change to allow for it / make it all work.
The only thing blocking it: Is config validation.

```py
diff --git a/homeassistant/helpers/config_validation.py b/homeassistant/helpers/config_validation.py
index bbf8475c53..698b6600b5 100644
--- a/homeassistant/helpers/config_validation.py
+++ b/homeassistant/helpers/config_validation.py
@@ -1599,7 +1599,7 @@ def determine_script_action(action: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
     if CONF_WAIT_TEMPLATE in action:
         return SCRIPT_ACTION_WAIT_TEMPLATE
 
-    if CONF_CONDITION in action:
+    if any(key in action for key in {CONF_CONDITION, "and", "or", "not"}):
         return SCRIPT_ACTION_CHECK_CONDITION
 
     if CONF_EVENT in action:
```

> The error in the second post is because it should be `entity_id`, not `entity`.
> 
 so sorry,
```
    action:
      - condition:
          - not:
              - condition: state
                entity_id: input_boolean.test_2
                state: 'on'
```
now doesnt error anymore

this:

```
    action:
      - not:
          - condition: state
            entity_id: input_boolean.test_2
            state: 'on'

```

still shows:
```
Logger: homeassistant.config
Source: config.py:454 
First occurred: 11:22:06 (1 occurrences) 
Last logged: 11:22:06

Invalid config for [automation]: Unable to determine action @ data['action'][0]. Got None. (See ?, line ?).```

Great!
The error you got (about `entit_id:`) is very unhelpful, and I'll see what can be done about that too.

> The error you got (about entit_id:) is very unhelpful, and I'll see what can be done about that too.

Or we just allow it and it ain't an issue 😄 

Honestly, thinking/playing it for a couple of hours now: I'm back to not understanding why we would block it / preventing it from working, while everything to support it is in place.

There are two issues here.

I meant the error
```
Unexpected value for condition: '[OrderedDict([('not', [OrderedDict([('condition', 'state'), ('entity', 'input_boolean.test_2'), ('state', 'on')])])])]'. Expected and, device, not, numeric_state, or, state, sun, template, time, trigger, zone, a list of conditions or a valid template @ data['action'][0]. Got None. (See ?, line ?).
``` 

That's unhelpful and won't go away. It's caused by the whole
```yaml
not:
  - condition: state
    entity: light.bed_light
```
being evaluated as a complete blob and gives the weird error above while
```yaml
condition: not
conditions:
  - condition: state
    entity: light.bed_light
```
would see this as an OK `not` condition, move on to checking `conditions` and raise an error that the `entity` key is not allowed.


About allowing `and`, `or` and `not` directy in the actions; sure, why not. I'm not strongly opposed to the idea.
By saying it was so by choice what I really meant was when I realized it wouldn't work I didn't put any effort into making it - not that I concously disabled it.
I even had your exact patch implemented at one point, but removed it.

> For reference, this was the change to allow for it / make it all work.
> The only thing blocking it: Is config validation.

~~There's also repeat, if and choose actions. Should it be considered there too?~~
Come to think of it - and without testing, it probably already works that way there...

>  it probably already works that way there...

Yup, it's all reused.

not sure what to say, but

```
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config] Invalid config for [automation]: Unable to determine action @ data['action'][0]. Got None. (See ?, line ?). 
```
 is back on:

```
    action:
      - not:
          - condition: state
            entity_id: input_boolean.test_2
            state: 'on'
```
I don't think anyone changed anything yet...
Made a PR to add it to consider it: <https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/71022>
just to confirm. thanks a lot!

review_comments: This means that none of the schemas below can have `and`, `or`, `not` as config parameters or else it will be marked as a condition.

Yes 🤷 

As they are logical operators already present in conditions now, I think that is OK. There are no current conflicts and worst case, if needed, the logic determining this can be extended/refined in the future to support cases otherwise (e.g., by changing detection order).
